title: Copies near users
summary: A CDN keeps copies of files and pages close to people, so your servers see far fewer requests.

steps.title: Do not cross the world for a picture
steps.text: A nearby copy saves the trip to origin only after it has the object. Try visitors at two different edges, then purge the copies.

steps.prompt: Twenty thousand people a second want the same pages. Protect your servers with a CDN.

between.note: A CDN sits between the browser and the servers, so pages are answered close to the visitor. Drop it onto that line.

steps.hint: Drag CDN between the browser and the servers.

rows.label: Typical CDN hit rate for static files
Sending data out to the internet

choices: Your users' passwords for safe keeping
A full working copy of your database
The code your servers run on
Copies of files and pages near users

steps.q: Which content is a poor fit for a CDN?
choices: A logo shown on every page of the site
A video that millions of people watch
A style sheet shared by every page
steps.why: Private data that differs per person should not be shared copies.

steps.q: What happens on a CDN miss?
choices: The request fails and the user retries
The CDN asks the user for the file
It goes to your servers, then is kept
The page is shown blank for a while
steps.why: The edge fetches from your origin, then keeps the copy for the next person.

takeaway: Put copies of shared content near people; keep your servers for what only they can do.
